source.title: An Attributional Theory of Achievement Motivation and Emotion

confidence_rationale: The foundational, field-defining theory that the TYPE of causal attribution (locus, stability, controllability) determines which emotion arises -- guilt specifically follows from internal + controllable attribution, shame from internal attribution to uncontrollable/global causes. This is the closest thing in the literature to a 'typed causal attribution governs moral emotion' law, directly grounding ARC-096's typed ontology and the attribution-precondition for ARC-097's guilt routing. Held at 0.7 because it is a theory of achievement emotion (success/failure) rather than interpersonal-harm morality per se, and is a theoretical framework rather than a single decisive experiment, so the mapping is by structural analogy.
failure_signatures: Weiner's controllability and locus dimensions are conceptually entangled with 'responsibility' in ways that are not fully separable -- a typed-attribution ontology that treats ownership tags (self/controllable/intentional) as cleanly orthogonal may over-formalise a distinction the source treats as partially overlapping.

The theory is built on achievement (success/failure) attributions; the guilt/shame mapping for interpersonal moral harm is an extension, so a system importing the dimensional structure wholesale risks mis-specifying which moral attributions yield guilt vs shame.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Perceived causes of outcomes vary along a small set of dimensions -- locus (internal/external), stability, and controllability (with intentionality/globality as further structures) -- and these dimensions, not the outcome itself, determine the emotional response. Controllability/personal-responsibility attributions are the key determinant of guilt and shame: guilt follows from attributing a negative outcome to an internal, controllable cause; shame follows from attributing it to an internal but uncontrollable (and often global) cause. Emotions so generated then guide motivated behaviour.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds ARC-096 (REE requires a typed causal-attribution ontology) by showing that, in humans, the TYPE of causal attribution is what selects the moral emotion -- i.e. you cannot get the right affect/route without first typing the cause (self/controllable/intentional vs uncontrollable/global). It also grounds the precondition structure of ARC-097: guilt-as-repair is licensed specifically by an internal+controllable (own-act, could-have-done-otherwise) attribution, which is exactly the ownership tag ARC-096 must supply before ARC-097's repair routing can fire.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Weiner's theory is about achievement emotions (reactions to success and failure), and the guilt/shame application is an extension within that framework rather than a dedicated theory of interpersonal moral harm. REE's attribution ontology is a richer typed set (self/world/body/model/commitment/other/shared/accidental/repairable) than Weiner's locus x stability x controllability cube, so the source supports the PRINCIPLE that attribution-type governs moral-emotional routing, not the specific REE tag set. The controllability/responsibility entanglement means the ownership tags may be less orthogonal in practice than a formal ontology assumes.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical synthesis in Psychological Review integrating a large body of human achievement-motivation and attribution experiments; the canonical statement of attribution theory of motivation and emotion.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (the field-defining theory, top venue, vast empirical base). Mapping fidelity moderate: it establishes the attribution-type -> emotion principle that ARC-096 needs, but via the achievement-emotion frame and a coarser dimensional set than REE's typed ontology. Transfer risk moderate from the achievement-to-moral-harm extension and theory-to-architecture mapping.
